Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a distinct, linear radiodense structure on the right side that parallels the normal ribs but is located within the thoracic cavity (intrathoracic), extending vertically from the upper to lower zones. This appearance and orientation are characteristic of an intrathoracic rib, a rare congenital anomaly, rather than pleural thickening or a vascular anomaly.
